chunks: A man said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'I have an estate in the mountain from which I profit three thousand dirhams every year. I spend two thousand dirhams of it on my dependants, and I give one thousand dirhams of it in charity every year.'

So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'If the two thousand suffices them for all that they need for their year, then you have been considerate for yourself, and been guided to your right conduct, and you have placed yourself during your lifetime at the status of what the living one bequeaths at his death.'

key_terms.ضَيْعَة: an agricultural estate or landholding generating income
key_terms.عِيَال: dependants (family members under one's financial care)
key_terms.وَصِيَّة: bequest, last will and testament made at death

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about dividing income between family expenses and charity?
ai.summary: A man informs Imam al-Baqir (AS) about his balanced financial practice: retaining two-thirds of his annual income for family needs and giving one-third in charity. The Imam praises this arrangement as long as the family portion is sufficient, comparing the practice to a deathbed bequest — commending the man for exercising foresight and generosity simultaneously during his lifetime. This teaching reflects the Imami tradition's approach to financial balance: neither excessive hoarding nor imprudent generosity, but rather a calculated care that considers one's obligations to dependants before charitable giving.
word_analysis: and you have been guided to success
